Article Title: Midterm blues: Why a 'lame' duck Donald Trump may push for a quick India-US trade deal
Article Text:
Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. (Image for representative purpose only)

What this means for India-US trade deal

What does Democrats’ win in US midterm elections mean for India-US trade deal prospects? Will Donald Trump be forced to change his strategy?The unfavourable midterm election outcome is unlikely to prompt President Donald Trump to change course on trade, according to an analysis by Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI).But, it’s important to note that both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing and the strengthening of supply chains.Democratic lawmakers, too, favour protective tariffs to safeguard unionised workers and local industries.“The adverse midterm results won’t change President Donald Trump’s trade direction because both Democrats and Republicans now favor economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing, and strong supply chains,” says Ajay Srivastava, founder of GTRI.Unable to rely on Congress for every measure, Trump is expected to continue exercising powers already available to the administration. These include Sections 232 and 301, along with executive orders, Treasury sanctions and rules issued by the Office of the United States Trade Representative (USTR), to exert unilateral pressure on trading partners.According to GTRI, with foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win.“Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout,” he says.For several months, leaders on both sides have indicated that a trade agreement is close to being finalised. However, the lack of clarity over the US offer appears to have held up its completion, the think tank says.Trump is now likely to use his executive authority to push India towards an early agreement that opens up the Indian market to American agricultural and industrial products, while securing other significant concessions for US businesses.The agreement under negotiation between India and the US is fundamentally different from the other free trade agreements (FTAs) India has entered into. Under conventional trade agreements, both participating countries reduce or eliminate their regular import duties, which are governed by World Trade Organization (WTO) rules and referred to as Most Favoured Nation (MFN) tariffs.The proposed US–India framework, however, follows a different approach. Washington would continue to levy its regular MFN duties, while India would be required to eliminate or lower such tariffs on most industrial products and a wide range of agricultural goods.The February 6 US–India Joint Statement sets out further commitments for India. These include aligning its security and economic policies with Washington, purchasing $500 billion worth of American goods over five years, and relaxing domestic regulatory oversight of imports from the US.“The US may be relying on the threat of additional tariffs to secure India's compliance. These include potential measures linked to India's purchases of Russian oil under the Graham Act and Section 301,” Srivastava notes.Also, signing the agreement would not necessarily protect India from further tariff action. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion.“India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement. Opening its markets, committing to large purchases and limiting its policy choices would carry lasting costs, while any U.S. tariff relief could prove temporary. New Delhi should insist on clear, enforceable reciprocal concessions, consistency with WTO rules and full freedom to protect its energy security and development priorities. The pressure to announce a deal must not outweigh the need to secure one that serves India’s long-term interests,” Srivastava says.
Article Summary: Both Democrats and Republicans have increasingly backed economic nationalism. The US could still impose additional duties of 15% to 18% over and above its standard MFN rates. In effect, the proposed arrangement would amount to economic coercion. India should not mistake relief from threatened tariffs for a balanced trade agreement.

Article Title: Elon Musk's nearly $500 million US midterm gamble backfires: Tesla, SpaceX stocks take a hit
Article Text:
Musk's political gamble falls flat, Tesla, SpaceX stocks take a hit

Why Musk's businesses could feel the political heat

Where Musk's $474 million election money went

Musk was not the only tech billionaire backing Trump

Elon Musk poured nearly half a billion dollars into the US midterm elections, but lost the gamble. As Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress and Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott in the Texas governor's race, shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure.Shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure, with SpaceX falling 3.8% in premarket trading and Tesla slipping 3.6%. Both stocks underperformed the broader market.The decline came even as US equities rallied following the midterm elections. The S&P 500 jumped 1.6%, gaining 119.7 points to close at 7,688.62. The Nasdaq Composite added 364.50 points, or 1.4%, to 25,736.51, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 1,569.40 points, or 3%, to 53,356.12. The Dow rose more than 1,500 points during the session.US stocks have historically tended to gain following midterm elections, regardless of which party wins. However, Musk's businesses moved in the opposite direction as the election results dealt a blow to the Republicans and US President Donald Trump, a close ally whom the billionaire helped elect.The setback is particularly significant given Musk's business interests in Texas, which houses his electric vehicle maker Tesla, his rocket-to-AI company SpaceX and a planned chipmaking venture between the two.His election spending was aimed at helping Republican candidates retain their positions and keeping Texas red.An analysis by The New York Times suggests that Musk contributed $474 million to Republican candidates during the 2026 midterms, including almost $224 million in Texas alone, making him the biggest donor of the election by a considerable margin.The Democratic victory could have significant implications for Musk's companies, particularly SpaceX's plans to build data centres. Slower approvals for these facilities could become a major hurdle as the company looks to tap the $28.5 trillion addressable market it presented to investors ahead of its IPO.With Democrats now controlling both chambers of Congress, analysts and experts expect greater scrutiny of data-centre projects and possible pushes for construction moratoriums amid growing local opposition over electricity costs.Musk has already faced scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers over restrictions on satellite communications used by Ukraine, mass federal job cuts at DOGE, and government contracts and subsidies flowing to his companies. The stronger Democratic presence in Congress could bring these issues back into focus.The latest market reaction also comes after a strong recovery in Tesla shares. The stock has rallied 34% since its late-July low, supported by investor optimism surrounding its artificial intelligence products and the potential combination with SpaceX.SpaceX, meanwhile, entered the ranks of the world's most valuable companies after going public earlier this year. The company generates billions of dollars through US government contracts, but its shares have largely remained flat since its June IPO, holding on to a massive $1.9 trillion market valuation.Musk's companies have previously shown sensitivity to election outcomes. Following Trump's re-election in 2024, Tesla shares surged more than 90% in little over a month. However, those gains later unwound as Musk's relationship with Trump soured and investors grew tired of his involvement in the Department of Government Efficiency.A significant portion of Musk's election spending flowed through political action committees supporting Republican candidates across the country.His America PAC, the super PAC he owns, received $216 million and was active in more than 40 House and Senate races. According to Newsweek, Musk contributed another $77 million to the group in the first half of October alone.The Senate Leadership Fund, the main super PAC backing Senate Republicans, received $168 million. Of this amount, $158 million was passed on to Texas PAC, the biggest supporter of Republican Ken Paxton.Musk also contributed $30 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund to help protect the Republican majority in the House. His trust gave another $10 million to Lone Star Liberty PAC, the main outside group supporting Paxton.His involvement in Republican fundraising is not new. In 2024, Musk spent nearly $300 million backing Trump and other Republican candidates.Musk's political contributions were the largest among four technology billionaires who backed Trump. Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, Michael Dell and Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff also supported the president through financial contributions, charitable commitments and White House projects.Ellison contributed around $45 million to a nonprofit supporting Trump's 2024 campaign, according to The Wall Street Journal. The donation remained undisclosed until June 2026. He later praised Trump at the White House event announcing the Stargate AI project, telling him, "We certainly couldn’t do this without you". Trump described Ellison as the "CEO of everything".Michael Dell and his wife Susan pledged $6.25 billion to fund "Trump Accounts". The money will go to the US Treasury and be deposited in $250 amounts into accounts for 25 million children aged 10 or younger. The programme targets children in zip codes where the median income is $150,000 or less. Trump later urged Americans to buy Dell computers, following which the company's stock rose more than 7%.Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff also backed Trump, marking a shift from his earlier political contributions, a major share of which went to Democrats. He committed $1 million towards Trump's White House ballroom, while Salesforce separately made two commitments of $1 million each. Benioff later faced criticism for supporting the deployment of National Guard troops in San Francisco, a proposal opposed by local city leaders. He subsequently withdrew his remarks and apologised for calling in the Guard.
Article Summary: Elon Musk poured nearly half a billion dollars into the US midterm elections. As Democrats seized control of both chambers of Congress, shares of Musk-owned companies came under pressure. SpaceX fell 3.8% in premarket trading and Tesla slipped 3.6%. Both stocks underperformed the broader market.

Article Title: Crude crashes below $100: Brent, WTI hit over two-month lows as Trump loses US midterm elections
Article Text:
Crude prices fall below $100 per barrel

Trump faces pressure as war weighs on Republicans

Qatar steps up mediation as Iran deal remains distant

Oil prices continued to ease on Thursday, with Brent crude and US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) tumbling below the $100-per-barrel threshold.Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90, as markets continued to react to the political fallout of the US midterm elections and the possibility of an end to the war with Iran.Brent crude futures fell 50 cents, or 0.53%, to $94.12 a barrel, while WTI crude declined 61 cents, or 0.69%, to $87.51.The latest movement follows Wednesday's sharp sell-off, when both benchmarks lost more than 8% and settled at their lowest levels in over two months. Brent ended the session at $94.62 a barrel, shedding $8.98 or 8.7%, while WTI settled at $88.12, down $7.97 or 8.3%. Both contracts recorded their lowest closing levels since August 31.The market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that US President Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.The election outcome has also complicated Washington's options in the conflict. With Democrats taking control of the House of Representatives and the Senate, Trump could find it harder to pursue further military action.Two sources close to Gulf government circles told Reuters that the weakened political position gave him greater reason to pursue a negotiated settlement, making a full-scale assault on Iran less likely.However, the possibility of a deal does not necessarily rule out further escalation. Gulf analysts said an agreement that allows Iran to claim a clear victory while leaving Trump appearing defeated could encourage recklessness rather than restraint.Trump told the Financial Times earlier this week that the US had no immediate plans to strike Iran. A day later, he acknowledged that the conflict had contributed to his party's sweeping defeat in the midterm elections.Vice president JD Vance also questioned the decision to enter the war on Wednesday, distancing himself from it and blaming the conflict entirely for the Republicans' electoral setback.Tehran, however, has indicated that a change in political control in Washington would not alter its position towards the US. Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei said in a written statement that American hostility would continue regardless of which party was in power.There were also fresh developments in the region, with Yemen's Houthis claiming to have targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.Diplomatic efforts to prevent another escalation have gathered pace, with Qatar stepping up mediation following the US elections. But the prospect of an immediate breakthrough remains uncertain.Meanwhile, regional energy flows continue to be disrupted. The United Arab Emirates is also looking at ways to reduce its reliance on the Strait of Hormuz, considering a third oil pipeline.Separately, US oil stockpiles recorded a decline last week. The Energy Information Administration said crude inventories dropped by 865,000 barrels to 409.8 million barrels in the week ended October 30. This was sharply different from expectations in a Reuters poll, where analysts had forecast an increase of 877,000 barrels.
Article Summary: Brent slipped below the $95-per-barrel mark, while WTI fell below $90. Market reaction came after Republicans lost control of Congress in the midterm elections, raising expectations that Donald Trump could face greater pressure to bring the US-Israeli war with Iran to an end.

Article Title: Trump tariff taxes Republicans: What US midterm results mean for Indian H-1B visa holders, Russian oil & trade deal
Article Text:
American voters have handed control of the US Congress to the opposition Democratic Party.

The results are expected to have implications extending beyond the US - so what does this mean for India? Let’s take a look:

What it means for H-1B visa holders and green card aspirants

India’s purchase of Russian oil

India-US trade deal & tariffs

US President Donald Trump has suffered a major blow in midterm elections with Republicans losing control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate.In a significant rebuke to Trump, American voters on Tuesday handed control of the US Congress to the opposition Democratic Party and shifted several key gubernatorial positions in closely watched elections.Trump's Republican Party suffered major defeats in its strongholds, including Texas, Georgia and Iowa, losing the governors' offices to Democratic candidates.Trump’s policies are being blamed by many as the reason for the loss - with tariffs and inflation in focus.US President Donald Trump has tightened access to H-1B visas through a $100,000 fee and a wage-weighted selection system, making it harder for Indian professionals to secure US jobs. His administration has also suspended eight technology companies from the PERM green card programme, disrupting some workers’ routes to permanent residency and green cards. So will the midterm results change that attitude?No. Not much is expected to change on this front, despite Trump’s loss. This is because both Democrats and Republicans prioritise domestic employment.According to Ajay Srivastava, founder of Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), tighter immigration policies find bipartisan support.“Be it the Biden administration or the Trump one, policies are increasingly becoming restrictive and that approach is unlikely to change,” Srivastava tells TOI.Also Read | ‘Death by restriction’: As Trump sours H-1B visa dream, which Indian IT professionals face the biggest hit? According to Rajiv Dabhadkar, Founder, National Organization For Software and Technology Professionals, the H-1B debate has moved beyond party politics to a fundamental US policy challenge: protecting American jobs while retaining access to global talent.“Regardless of the outcome of the midterm elections, the US is looking to address long-standing flaws in the immigration system, including wage protections, worker displacement and how employers use foreign professionals,” he tells TOI.What fundamentally needs to be understood is that H-1B reform is now a bipartisan American policy imperative, not merely a political reaction to one administration, he adds.Earlier this year, the Donald Trump administration managed to get support for the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026. The Act allows the US President to impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries importing oil from Russia and Iran in a big way.India and China lead the lot of Russian oil buyers. Recently, Trump announced a waiver on those tariffs for India. But, it’s important to note that the waiver was only for a period of 60 days.Also Read | Does Trump’s 60-day tariff waiver really give relief to India? What it means for US trade deal & oil prices The Republicans losing control of the Congress is unlikely to change the Trump administration’s stance on buyers of Russian crude oil. This is because the bill enjoyed bipartisan support - both Democrats and Republicans appear keen to penalise buyers of Russian oil.However, what may work in India’s favour for now is America’s own diesel deal with Russia and the need by the Trump administration and even the Democrats to keep oil prices in check. Sanctioning Russian oil or penalising buyers of Moscow’s crude will not help that cause.So, for now India continues to enjoy relief from the prospect of 100% tariffs for its crude oil procurement from Russia, but this may work as a pressure tactic by the US to finalise a trade deal.For India, which is still negotiating a trade agreement with the United States, the outcome of the midterm elections could strengthen the case for taking a cautious, wait-and-watch approach.Earlier this month, Commerce minister Piyush Goyal said the first phase of the India-US trade agreement was in the final stages of drafting. However, he stressed that New Delhi would move ahead only if the terms gave Indian exporters an edge over their competitors.India and the US have already finalised a framework for the first phase of the Bilateral Trade Agreement. However, changes in the US tariff environment have led to further negotiations. India is seeking tariff rates on its exports that are more favourable than those faced by competing countries.In the meantime, experts believe the midterm setback could prompt Trump to pursue an early trade agreement with India. They said that with Washington struggling to exercise foreign policy leverage over Russia, China and Iran, Trump may look for quick success on the trade front.However, the economic think tank GTRI said the unfavourable midterm outcome was unlikely to fundamentally alter Trump's trade policy. Both Republicans and Democrats, it noted, support economic nationalism, domestic manufacturing and robust supply chains."With foreign policy leverage failing against Russia, China, and Iran, Trump needs a quick win. Expect heightened pressure on India for a trade deal to prove American clout and the midterm losses may push Trump to seek a quick India trade deal," said Ajay Srivastava.Federation of Indian Export Organisations (FIEO) president SC Ralhan said the US continues to be an important destination for Indian goods and services."What will matter to Indian exporters in the months ahead is how US policy on tariffs and market access takes shape. MSMEs in particular need predictable trading conditions to price orders confidently and plan shipments months in advance," he told PTI.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump has suffered a major blow in midterm elections. Republicans lost control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate. The results are expected to have implications extending beyond the US. So what does this mean for India? Let’s take a look.

Article Title: Gold, silver price outlook: US-Iran tensions, inflation data to set the tone next week
Article Text:
Gold and silver price outlook

Inflation data and Fed commentary in focus

Gold and silver recover after a volatile week

Bargain buying supports recovery, but gains remain limited

NEW DELHI: Gold and silver may have ended the week on a brighter note, but whether they can keep the shine going is another question. Bullion prices could remain under pressure next week as investors brace for a busy mix of inflation data, crude oil movements and fresh twists in the US-Iran conflict.Both precious metals managed to finish the week with gains in domestic and international markets. However, the recovery may not be enough to signal a sustained turnaround. Investors will be keeping a close eye on inflation readings from major economies for clues on the interest rate outlook, while geopolitical tensions and peace negotiations could add to the uncertainty.With several factors pulling prices in different directions, will gold and silver find their footing or face another bout of volatility?Here are the key triggers to watch next week.A series of inflation releases from China, the US, Germany, Japan and India will be closely watched by investors. The readings could provide clues about the direction of interest rates and influence sentiment towards precious metals.Speeches by Federal Reserve officials and US employment data will also remain on the market's radar. Investors will assess these developments alongside movements in crude oil prices to gauge the broader economic outlook."Gold and silver's momentum remains down as investors will focus on the inflation data from China, the US, Germany, Japan, India, etc along with some Fed officials' commentary," said Pranav Mer, senior vice president, EBG - Commodity & currency research, JM Financial Services Ltd.Chinese economic indicators will also be important, particularly for industrial metals, analysts said.Geopolitical developments are likely to remain another major factor for bullion prices. US President Donald Trump confirmed fresh military strikes on Iran but also said Washington had made "a lot of progress" in negotiations with Tehran.The developments have left investors tracking both the conflict and the possibility of a diplomatic resolution.Mer said markets would also watch progress in peace negotiations between the US and Iran to end the war, as well as the Russia-Ukraine peace talks.The domestic and international bullion markets recorded weekly gains, despite facing pressure earlier in the week.On the Multi Commodity Exchange, December gold futures rose Rs 3,682, or nearly 3%, over the past week to close at Rs 1.42 lakh per 10 grams. Silver futures gained Rs 5,655, or 3.15%, to settle at Rs 1.84 lakh per kilogram.Overseas, Comex gold futures for December delivery advanced $176, or 4.5%, to close at $4,074.9 per ounce. Silver futures climbed $2.6, or 5.4%, to settle at $51.94 per ounce.Explaining the price movement, Mer said stronger-than-expected US nonfarm payroll data and improving consumer sentiment initially weighed on bullion. These developments lifted the dollar and Treasury yields, putting pressure on gold and silver."However, prices ended with a strong weekly gain of more than 4 per cent in global markets, following a sharp rally mid-week after the US midterm election outcome that showed Democrats sweeping wins in both the Senate and the House over the Republicans," he added.Precious metals found support during the week as investors bought at lower price levels and traders covered short positions. However, a correction in industrial metals, particularly copper, restricted the gains.The decline in AI, data centre and technology stocks across global markets, especially in the US, also supported bullion by encouraging demand for safe-haven assets.The recovery, however, faced another bout of selling towards the end of the week. According to Mer, gold and silver futures came under pressure on Friday, closing at around $4,074 and $52 per ounce, respectively.Domestic bullion prices could see moderate fluctuations next week as traders respond to international price movements, currency changes and inflation trends.Festive demand around Diwali will also be among the factors influencing domestic trading. The commodity market will remain closed during the morning session on Tuesday due to Diwali-Balipratipada.
Article Summary: Both precious metals managed to finish the week with gains in domestic and international markets. Investors will be keeping a close eye on inflation readings from major economies for clues on interest rate outlook. Speeches by Federal Reserve officials and US employment data will also remain on the market's radar.

Article Title: India's clean energy push cut its fuel import bill by $240 billion: IEA
Article Text:
India's renewable energy push could save $240 billion

Consistent policies helping India attract clean energy investments

India could save $240 billion on coal and gas imports by 2030

Solar to lead renewable energy expansion

India's shift towards renewable energy could help it save billions on fuel imports, while making the country less dependent on global energy markets.The transition could bring cumulative savings of nearly $240 billion on coal and natural gas imports by 2030, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA).As India expands its clean energy capacity, the benefits are going beyond sustainability. The move is also strengthening the country's energy security and economic resilience. IEA executive director Fatih Birol said India's experience could offer useful lessons for other emerging economies looking to expand renewable energy.In a post on X, Birol said India's renewable energy expansion was helping the country deal with uncertainty in global energy markets by reducing its dependence on imported fossil fuels."India’s renewables expansion is delivering major energy security benefits amid heightened uncertainty in global energy markets," Birol said.He added that India's experience demonstrated "how consistent policies can help drive down renewable energy costs and attract investment, offering valuable lessons for other emerging economies".Birol was responding to a post by Union minister for new and renewable energy Prahlad Joshi, who highlighted the economic benefits of India's renewable energy transition.Joshi said the shift was not just about making energy cleaner. It was also strengthening India's energy security and economic resilience by reducing import dependence and conserving foreign exchange.The minister shared an report on the IEA's India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026, which estimated that India's cumulative savings on coal and natural gas imports could approach $240 billion by 2030.This projection assumes that fuel prices remain broadly in line with their 2024-25 averages.The savings are also expected to make a significant difference to India's annual import bill. The report projected that annual savings on fossil fuel imports could reach around $35 billion by 2030. This would be higher than the country's actual non-coking coal and natural gas import bill in FY 2024-25.Solar and wind power are expected to account for most of these savings. Solar photovoltaic power could contribute nearly 60 per cent of the projected cumulative savings, while wind power could account for almost 30 per cent.India's renewable energy capacity could reach around 530 GW by 2030, according to the IEA's projections. Solar power is expected to drive much of this growth, with its capacity projected to exceed 350 GW.However, generating more renewable electricity is only part of the task. The agency has highlighted the need for continued investment in transmission infrastructure, energy storage and power system flexibility to accommodate the growing share of renewable electricity.Birol's remarks highlight how India's clean energy expansion is helping strengthen energy security while offering the possibility of substantial savings on fuel imports. The country's experience with consistent policies, lower renewable energy costs and investment could also provide useful lessons for other emerging economies.
Article Summary: India could save $240 billion on coal and natural gas imports by 2030. IEA executive director Fatih Birol said India's experience could offer useful lessons for other emerging economies looking to expand renewable energy. Solar and wind power are expected to account for most of these savings.

Article Title: Samsung set to become South Korea's first company with 200 trillion won in cash
Article Text:
Samsung's cash reserves to cross 200 trillion won as AI chip demand grows

Samsung Electronics is on course to become the first company in South Korea to build cash assets of more than 200 trillion won ($146.6 billion), with the artificial intelligence (AI)-driven semiconductor boom strengthening its financial position.The chipmaker's cash reserves have nearly doubled over the past year, while its overall assets have also grown. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. This marks a rise of 24.8 trillion won from the 190 trillion won recorded at the end of the previous quarter, as reported by Yonhap news agency.The latest estimate is also almost twice the 108.5 trillion won the company held at the end of the third quarter of 2025.Samsung's total assets stood at 791.8 trillion won at the end of September, an increase of 32.4 trillion won over the preceding three months.The company's growing cash position is expected to be enough to cover the highest possible payout under its landmark shareholder return policy announced in August, market watchers estimate.Samsung had indicated that it would make between 90 trillion won and 110 trillion won available for shareholder returns in 2026.The company is also expected to announce its shareholder policy for the coming year at a board meeting scheduled for January.Alongside shareholder payouts, Samsung is preparing for a significant increase in spending on its semiconductor business.Investments in chipmaking infrastructure and research and development are expected to exceed 100 trillion won this year, marking a historic high. Of this amount, 84.4 trillion won is expected to go towards expanding its memory production facilities.Samsung expects the semiconductor supercycle to extend through next year, supported by continued investments in artificial intelligence and a crunch in memory supply.
Article Summary: Samsung's cash and cash equivalents are estimated to have reached 214.8 trillion won by the end of the third quarter, according to industry data released on Sunday. The increase comes as Samsung prepares for higher investments in semiconductor manufacturing and research, alongside a sizeable shareholder return programme.

Article Title: Indian Oil plans to buy its own oil, LPG ships as freight costs surge 4 times
Article Text:
Strait of Hormuz disruptions push IOC to acquire crude oil, LPG carriers

Shipping costs jump as Hormuz disruptions tighten the squeeze

Russia accounts for 55% of IOC's crude sourcing

Crude prices climb to around $120 per barrel in October

Inventory gains help IOC report Rs 21,630 crore profit

With shipping costs rising sharply and movement around the Strait of Hormuz facing disruptions, Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) is looking to take greater control of how its crude oil and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) reach its refineries.The state-owned oil major plans to purchase its own carriers and is also exploring the possibility of getting ships built in India.IOC's board has approved the purchase of a few vessels, and tenders for the proposed acquisitions were issued several months ago, director of finance Anuj Jain said during the company's second-quarter earnings call."The country needs oil sector companies to focus more on the shipping area now," Jain said, adding that the company was examining shipbuilding opportunities in India under the government's Make in India initiative.The proposed purchases could change the way IOC manages its shipping requirements. The company has traditionally depended on time-chartered and voyage-chartered vessels but is now looking at a combination of owning ships, improving existing charter arrangements and encouraging domestic shipbuilding.The rising cost of transporting crude oil and LPG has made shipping arrangements an important part of IOC's strategy.Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East have disrupted commercial movement near the Strait of Hormuz, leading to higher freight rates and war-risk insurance costs.IOC currently has three crude oil carriers and nine LPG vessels under time-charter arrangements. These have helped it contain transportation expenses during the current crisis, Jain said.The difference between chartered and spot-market rates has been particularly sharp. IOC pays around $2-2.50 per barrel for its time-chartered crude carriers, against spot-market rates of up to $8-10 per barrel.The pressure is even more pronounced in LPG transportation. Freight rates that would generally be around $40 per tonne have climbed to $160-180 per tonne in the spot market, Jain said.Alongside its plans to strengthen shipping capacity, IOC has changed the geographical mix of its crude purchases to diversify supplies and limit exposure to disruptions.Russia supplied 55 per cent of the company's crude requirements in the first half of the current financial year. Middle Eastern countries accounted for another 24 per cent, while Africa contributed around 10 per cent.Brazil supplied 7 per cent of IOC's crude, the United States accounted for 2-5 per cent and Venezuela contributed 3-4 per cent, Jain said.The company has also moved towards greater reliance on spot purchases. These accounted for around 87 per cent of its crude sourcing in the first half of FY27, against approximately 50 per cent in the previous financial year.IOC has managed to negotiate discounts against benchmark prices despite fluctuations in the global market. The premium or discount paid over benchmark crude during the September quarter ranged from a discount of $5 per barrel to a premium of $12 per barrel. In the preceding quarter, the range was between zero and a premium of $18 per barrel.Jain said IOC continued to purchase Russian crude at what it described as optimal prices and was also processing Venezuelan crude.The company's procurement strategy comes amid a sharp rise in oil prices following the escalation of US-Iran hostilities towards the end of February.Indian basket crude, which averaged around $65-70 per barrel in February, stayed above $100 for much of the first quarter. It averaged approximately $120 per barrel in October, Jain said.Despite the supply-chain challenges, IOC has kept its refinery operations at optimal levels while building up inventories to provide a buffer against disruptions.Its crude oil inventory has increased to around 39 days from the usual 33-35 days. The company was also holding 20 days of LPG inventory and 23-25 days of petrol and diesel stocks.IOC's net profit rose to Rs 21,630 crore in the September quarter, compared with a loss of Rs 2,661 crore in the preceding quarter. The company had reported a profit of Rs 7,610 crore in the corresponding period last year.Inventory gains and improved performance across several businesses contributed to the quarterly profitability, the company said.IOC recorded a gross refining margin of $18.52 per barrel, excluding the impact of the special additional excise duty. Its inventory gain stood at Rs 6,948 crore during the quarter.However, the company continues to face uncertainty from geopolitical developments. Jain said these remained a key concern, particularly because of their impact on crude procurement, freight costs and marketing margins.IOC's plans to acquire vessels and explore shipbuilding in India come as it looks to strengthen its control over transportation alongside diversifying its crude purchases.
Article Summary: IOC plans to purchase its own carriers and is also exploring the possibility of getting ships built in India. The company's board has approved the purchase of a few vessels, and tenders for the proposed acquisitions were issued several months ago. Russia supplied 55% of the company's crude requirements in the first half of the current financial year.

Article Title: Gold, Muhurat trading and big business: The economics of Diwali and how they've changed
Article Text:
For generations, Diwali has been associated with distinctive business, financial and economic traditions that continue to evolve with changing times.

An occasion for wealth creation

Inculcating regular investment habits

GenZ's new traditions

Red account books to digital ledgers

bahi-khatas

Shubh

Labh

Diwali traditions linked to finances

bahi-khatas

Dhanteras and the gold rush: Buying precious metals

The gold rush in festive season

The Diwali economy: Where does India's festive money go?

Festive shopping: Online vs offline

Muhurat trading : When Diwali meets the stock market

How have markets performed?

Experts decode: What the festive season tells us about India's economy

A more selective household wallet

The wider economic impact

How festive season supports businesses

Financial discipline

From auspicious trades to long-term investing

Festive trends versus lasting shifts

K-shaped economy

Takeaway

Diwali is more than a festival of lights. For generations, it has also been an occasion for Indian businesses, traders and households to review their finances, begin new accounts, buy gold and make investments.While these customs have retained their significance, the way people observe them has evolved. Physical account books have given way to digital ledgers, gold purchases now include investment-oriented products, and younger investors are exploring financial markets.Here is how five Diwali traditions connect culture, commerce and India's economy.Diwali has traditionally been associated with prosperity and the worship of Goddess Lakshmi, the deity of wealth. For households, it is an occasion to buy valuables, purchase gold, set aside savings and plan finances for the year ahead.Wealth creation is no longer limited to physical assets. Alongside gold and traditional savings instruments, households are exploring mutual funds, shares and other financial products. Diwali or Dhanteras can also serve as a starting point for investing.Dr Shunil Tripathi, an NCFE trainer empanelled with the RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA, said festivals can provide a cultural and emotional motivation to move from saving to investing.The challenge is to turn an occasional decision into a regular habit through financial awareness and long-term planning.“The basic philosophy, however, remains similar: save today to secure tomorrow,” he said.Younger investors may mark the occasion by starting a mutual fund systematic investment plan (SIP), buying Gold ETFs or opening a Demat account. These serve different purposes: a SIP enables regular investment, while a Demat account holds securities. The larger shift is towards using the festival to think about long-term financial goals.For many Indian trading communities, particularly in Gujarat, Diwali marks the beginning of a new business year. One prominent tradition is Chopda Pujan, the ritual of worshipping account books before beginning a fresh set of financial records.Traditionally, business families closed old accounts and worshipped newduring Lakshmi Puja. The books were marked with auspicious words such asand, symbolising prosperity and a fresh beginning.The practice continues in some families, even as formal accounting has shifted to digital systems. GST has added to businesses' formal record-keeping and compliance obligations, including maintaining transaction records, issuing tax invoices and filing periodic returns. Accounting software and digital ledgers are now part of routine operations.There is also an important distinction between customary Diwali-to-Diwali reviews and statutory accounting. Financial reporting, income-tax filings and GST compliance follow the April-to-March financial year. Some traditional businesses nevertheless maintainalongside formal records and compare their net worth from one Diwali to the next. Net worth is calculated by subtracting liabilities from assets.Chartered accountant Balvinder Singh Oberoi said festive-period sales were another important measure. “One financial metric they do track religiously is festive period sales,” he said, referring to businesses comparing sales during the Diwali period with the corresponding period a year earlier.Buying gold on Dhanteras is among India's most enduring festive traditions. Associated with prosperity, security and wealth preservation, the occasion is particularly important for jewellery retailers, bullion dealers and precious-metal businesses.Buying patterns are evolving. Consumers are showing interest in lightweight designs, smaller denominations of gold coins and bars, and exchanges of old gold for new jewellery. High prices have encouraged some buyers to adapt the size and design of their purchases rather than abandon the tradition.This year's Dhanteras, observed on November 6, brought fresh momentum for jewellers as gold prices eased from record levels. Reuters reported local gold prices at around Rs 1,41,800 per 10 grams on Friday, after falling to Rs 1,37,863 earlier in the week, their lowest level since March 24. The correction brought some buyers who had been waiting for more favourable rates back to jewellery stores ina addition to those who waited for the cultural significance.The All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC), in a preliminary assessment after Dhanteras, estimated gold sales at around Rs 60,000 crore, up 15-20% in value terms from the previous year. Volumes were expected to remain broadly unchanged, suggesting that higher prices accounted for much of the increase in sales value.Demand also extended to diamond jewellery, with wedding shoppers and families contributing to purchases.Demand for diamond jewellery also reportedly grew 25-30% during the festive period.The festive season is a crucial consumption period for several industries. Alongside FMCG, automobiles, consumer durables, jewellery and apparel, spending also benefits travel, hospitality and premium gifting. Ecommerce has also been a key contributor in this aspect, allowing quick deliveries, festival sales and wide variety.Ravi Kapoor, partner and leader for the retail and consumer sector at PwC India, included travel and premium gifting among the categories that gain from festive demand. He pointed to the long holiday period as a reason more families are open to travelling. “A lot of families actually now are quite open for travel,” he said.Kapoor estimated that “in automobiles roughly a quarter to 30% of volumes happen in this period”. He added: “Same is the number for durables. 30 to 40% durables get sold right.”The demand story is also spreading beyond metropolitan households. Kapoor said e-commerce, digital payments and better physical infrastructure had widened access to consumers in smaller cities and towns. “The access has become much, much better, much easier,” he said, pointing to the growing contribution of Tier-II and Tier-III markets to new online customers.However, higher festive sales do not automatically mean that households have become more financially comfortable. The source of the spending matters: purchases supported by improved incomes and savings may point to stronger consumption, while those financed by stretching household budgets may be harder to sustain.Economist Dr Rohit Kumar Singh said this distinction was central to assessing demand. “Are households spending more because their incomes and savings have improved, or are they stretching their budgets to make room for festive purchases?” he asked.Anand Ramanathan, partner and consumer industry leader at Deloitte South Asia, also highlighted the gap between financial confidence and spending capacity. Deloitte's March 2026 ConsumerSignals survey found that 79% of Indian consumers were confident about meeting upcoming payments and 60% were comfortable with their savings. However, only 65% were willing to make large purchases, down five percentage points from the previous month. Just 43% said they could afford to spend on things that brought them joy.The findings suggest that financial confidence does not always translate into a willingness to make discretionary purchases. Whether consumers continue spending after the festive season will be a better test of how durable the demand is.Diwali's association with wealth and prosperity also extends to India's stock markets. Every year, the BSE and NSE hold a special trading session on Diwali, known as Muhurat trading, marking the beginning of the new Samvat year.Many investors consider the session auspicious and use it to make a symbolic investment or begin a longer-term investment plan. The tradition dates back to the BSE's introduction of the session in 1957; the NSE began holding it in 1992.Both the Sensex and Nifty closed higher in eight of the last 10 Muhurat trading sessions from 2016 to 2025. The two exceptions were 2016 and 2017. The indices then recorded eight consecutive positive sessions from 2018 through 2025. In the 2025 session, the Sensex gained 63 points, while the Nifty rose 25 points.These gains, however, reflect movement during a single special session, not returns over the full Samvat year. An auspicious start does not guarantee market gains. Investors still need to assess companies, understand their risk appetite and maintain a diversified portfolio.Muhurat trading brings together faith and finance, giving the stock market a cultural connection beyond its regular trading calendar. The more meaningful step is to carry the discipline of that beginning into the rest of the year.Diwali sales offer a snapshot of India's consumption economy, but the festive rush also raises larger questions. Is spending broad-based or concentrated among affluent households? Are consumers buying more, or simply paying higher prices? And does the demand generated during the festive season translate into sustained growth for businesses?Anand Ramanathan, partner and consumer industry leader at Deloitte South Asia, said India's festive consumption story reflected a larger market but more selective spending. Consumers are reallocating budgets towards purchases they consider worthwhile.“The story is increasingly one of a larger consumption economy combined with a more selective household wallet,” he said.Smaller discretionary purchases are increasingly spread throughout the year, while big-ticket items such as appliances and electronics remain linked to festive discounts and financing. Food, sweets and entertaining, meanwhile, generate occasion-led demand. Ramanathan described Diwali as “a blend of accelerated demand and occasion-created consumption”.Economist Dr Rohit Kumar Singh said festive demand supports more than retailers. Manufacturers, transporters, warehouses, packaging companies and MSMEs also benefit, while seasonal hiring creates temporary employment. “The festive season also supports a much wider network of businesses. Manufacturers, transporters, warehouses, packaging companies and MSMEs all benefit from the increase in activity,” he said. However, smaller businesses can face unsold inventory, delayed payments and working-capital pressure. Higher input costs, including crude oil, can further squeeze margins.Dr Shunil Tripathi, the NCFE trainer empanelled with RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and PFRDA, said Diwali could be an opportunity to review income, expenditure, savings, investments and financial goals. Traditional practices of setting aside money, grains or gold reflected the idea of preparing for the future. “The basic philosophy, however, remains similar: save today to secure tomorrow,” he said. But social pressure and the desire to keep up with others can also lead to unnecessary purchases and borrowing.Chartered accountant Balvinder Singh Oberoi said the symbolic investment made during Muhurat trading could be a starting point for greater financial awareness. “Muhurat trading provides that crucial first step to getting started,” he said. The real value lies in using the occasion to understand markets and build a consistent, long-term investment habit rather than treating a token purchase as wealth creation.Ravi Kapoor, partner and leader for the retail and consumer sector at PwC India, cautioned against treating every festive-season trend as a permanent change in consumption. One structural shift, he said, was the movement from unbranded to branded products, including in categories such as sarees, jewellery and food.“The long term consumption story is very clearly the growth of formal consumption, the growth of formal economy in the country,” he said.Kapoor also described India as an “E-shaped economy”, with affluent households relatively insulated from economic changes, middle-income consumers spending cautiously and lower-income groups facing tighter constraints. Whether festive demand continues after Diwali, and whether the shift towards organised brands persists, will offer a better indication of the economy's underlying consumption trends.Ultimately, Diwali's economic significance goes beyond a surge in shopping or a promising start to the business year. It brings together consumption, investment and traditional practices, while offering a window into changing household priorities. Whether this festive momentum translates into sustained demand and long-term financial discipline will become clearer in the months ahead.
Article Summary: For generations, Diwali has been associated with distinctive business, financial and economic traditions that continue to evolve with changing times. Physical account books have given way to digital ledgers, gold purchases now include investment-oriented products, and younger investors are exploring financial markets.

Article Title: FIIs return to Dalal Street, pump Rs 38,971 crore into Indian equities amid AI sell-off
Article Text:
FIIs pour in Dalal Street after global AI stocks tumble

Global tech stocks face heavy selling

Why India is attracting foreign investors

FPIs turn buyers while DIIs continue selling

NEW DELHI: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have invested Rs 38,971 crore in Indian equities this week, as a sharp fall in global technology stocks flipped investment trends.Concerns over heavy spending on artificial intelligence (AI) and a possible slowdown in data centre investments have triggered selling across global markets, making Dalal Street more attractive to foreign investors.Overseas investors had earlier been selling Indian shares as money moved towards AI-focused markets, according to NSDL. However, the recent fall in AI stocks has led to a change in strategy, with foreign investors returning to Indian equities.Global markets came under pressure on Thursday, with losses continuing on Friday. In the US, a sharp fall in technology stocks wiped out gains made during Wall Street's post-election rally.All three major US indices recorded their biggest single-day losses since April 2025 on Thursday. This erased the gains from Wednesday, when the Dow jumped more than 1,500 points, marking its best trading session since April 2025.The sell-off was driven by concerns that spending on AI-related data centres could slow down. These concerns also affected other AI-focused markets, including South Korea, Taiwan and Japan.V K Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments Limited, said that decline in AI stocks in the US and other markets had played a key role in bringing foreign investors back to India.He said concerns over data centre spending in the US were behind the sell-off. The Democrats, who won both chambers of Congress, are opposed to indiscriminate spending on data centres and are expected to demand safeguards for AI.As investors reassess their investments in AI-focused markets, India has become a more attractive option."The AI sell-off has made India, which is widely regarded as a non-AI trade, attractive for FPIs. Furthermore, the impressive earnings growth in India and the attractive large-cap valuations made India a favoured investment destination," Vijayakumar said.The return of foreign investors also brought a change in the buying and selling patterns of institutional investors. While FPIs turned aggressive buyers, domestic institutional investors (DIIs) remained sellers on all trading days last week.Vijayakumar said the sudden change in investment trends and a short squeeze helped push the market higher."Last week the market witnessed a sudden and complete role reversal from institutions - FPIs turned aggressive buyers, and DIIs turned sellers on all days. The aggressive buying by the FPIs and the consequent short squeeze triggered a big rally in the market, pushing up the Nifty by 7.58% in a week," he said.He added that foreign investors were buying heavily in some of the biggest companies listed on the market, particularly in the financial, IT, automobile and telecom sectors."FIIs have turned major buyers in index heavy weights in financials, IT, automobiles and telecom," he said.The Nifty rose 7.58% over the week as foreign investors increased their purchases. India's earnings growth and large-cap valuations have also added to its appeal at a time when global investors are reconsidering their exposure to AI-related investments.
Article Summary: Overseas investors had earlier been selling Indian shares as money moved towards AI-focused markets. The recent fall in AI stocks has led to a change in strategy, with foreign investors returning to Indian equities. FIIs have turned major buyers in index heavy weights in financials, IT, automobiles and telecom.

Article Title: Samvat 2083 outlook: Stocks, sectors and levels investors should keep an eye on
Article Text:
Samvat 2083: What's next for investors?

India's growth outlook remains encouraging

Which sectors could offer opportunities in Samvat 2083?

Muhurat trading: Why experts advise a cautious approach

Nifty support and resistance levels to watch

(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market and other asset classes given by experts are their own. These opinions do not represent the views of The Times of India)

NEW DELHI: Diwali is here, and investors are looking ahead to Samvat 2083 with one key question: what lies ahead for Dalal Street in the new year? While India's domestic growth outlook remains encouraging, global uncertainties and market volatility could keep investors on their toes. Market participants are therefore advising investors to be selective with their stock choices and keep their return expectations realistic.Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund expects moderate returns from equities in the coming Samvat. In its annual 'Muhurat Picks Samvat 2083' presentation, the fund house advised investors to focus on quality companies, maintain a balanced portfolio and stay invested for the long term rather than chase short-term market rallies.It also cautioned that geopolitical tensions, changes in crude oil prices and the cautious approach of global central banks could keep markets volatile over the coming year. A long-term investment approach, it said, would help investors navigate these uncertainties.Despite global concerns, India's domestic growth outlook remains positive. Kotak Mutual Fund expects the country's GDP to grow 7.1% in FY27, with domestic demand continuing to support corporate earnings.High-frequency indicators also point to a broad-based economic recovery.However, the fund house believes investors should not expect exceptionally high equity returns in the new Samvat. Moderate returns, it said, are a more realistic expectation for the broader market.There is also some valuation comfort in large-cap and mid-cap stocks. According to Kotak Mutual Fund's presentation, major market indices were trading below their long-term average valuations as of October 31, 2026.This comes after an uneven performance across equity market segments since the previous Diwali. Data covering October 20, 2025, to October 31, 2026, showed divergent movements in the Nifty 50 TRI, Nifty Midcap 150 TRI and Nifty Smallcap 250 TRI, with mid-cap and small-cap stocks experiencing sharper volatility during the period.Meanwhile, analysts at domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOSL) said Nifty valuations were attractive at 17.5 times forward earnings, around 16% below the long-term average. Small-cap stocks, however, continued to trade at a 25% premium to their historical average.The brokerage expects earnings growth to recover over the coming years. Nifty earnings per share are projected to rise 16% and 14% year-on-year in FY27 and FY28, respectively, compared with 5% in FY26.For the new Samvat, market experts favour banking and financial services, capital markets, manufacturing, global outsourcing and exports, consumption and digital businesses.They also see opportunities in healthcare devices, aerospace, auto components, pharmaceutical ingredients, garments, port cargo, organised jewellery and quick-commerce platforms.Against this backdrop, Kotak Mutual Fund's investment strategy centres on identifying quality companies and maintaining disciplined asset allocation. The fund house has advised investors to remain focused on their long-term investment goals instead of trying to benefit from short-term market movements.It has also recommended that investors align their mutual fund choices with their individual risk profiles and seek guidance from financial advisors before making investment decisions.As investors prepare for the special Diwali trading session on Sunday, market experts have called for a cautious, stock-specific approach. With benchmark indices approaching key resistance levels, limited liquidity during the session could amplify market movements, they said.Muhurat trading is traditionally considered an auspicious occasion to begin investments and review financial portfolios. However, experts have cautioned investors against making impulsive decisions driven by festive sentiment. Instead, they have advised them to focus on company fundamentals, valuations and long-term financial goals.The approach, experts said, should differ depending on the investment horizon. Long-term investors can use the occasion to review their asset allocation and selectively accumulate fundamentally strong stocks. Short-term traders, meanwhile, should monitor technical levels and global cues before taking positions.For those entering the stock market for the first time, experts recommend starting with small investments in fundamentally strong companies and adopting a long-term holding approach. They have also advised against buying stocks simply because the occasion is considered auspicious.Given the possibility of lower liquidity during the limited trading session, investors should avoid placing large orders or trading aggressively, experts added.The cautious approach also comes as both benchmark indices approach crucial resistance zones following a recent rally. Market experts expect trading to remain sideways to consolidative during the Muhurat session.Trading around 24,600, Nifty has immediate support at 24,350, while resistance is placed in the 24,700-24,800 range.Experts have also flagged the possibility of profit booking after six consecutive sessions of gains. Geopolitical concerns, crude oil volatility and weakness in global markets could add to the pressure.As Samvat 2083 begins, the broader advice for investors is to keep return expectations realistic, remain selective with stock choices and stick to disciplined investment strategies rather than get carried away by short-term market movements.
Article Summary: Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund expects moderate returns from equities in the coming Samvat. The fund house advised investors to focus on quality companies, maintain a balanced portfolio and stay invested for the long term. Despite global concerns, India's domestic growth outlook remains positive.

Article Title: Delhi, Mumbai lead festive rush as 57 lakh passengers take trains in November
Article Text:
Festive rush sees 57 lakh passengers leave major cities through 16 railway stations in six days

NEW DELHI: Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Surat recorded the highest outward passenger movement during the current festive rush, with around 57 lakh passengers travelling from 16 railway stations across these regions between November 1 and 6, according to railway ministry data.Around 30 lakh of these passengers had reserved tickets, while another 27 lakh travelled in unreserved classes.The passenger outflow was nearly 20 lakh higher than the combined traffic of around 37 lakh recorded during September and October across these five regions, highlighting the sharp surge in travel demand during the festive period. Delhi and Mumbai accounted for the largest share of the departures.The surge was also reflected in the average daily footfall at major railway stations between November 1 and 5. Delhi recorded the highest daily footfall, at around 8 lakh passengers, against its earlier average of 5 lakh. Hyderabad saw daily numbers rise to 4 lakh from 2.5 lakh, while Bengaluru recorded 3.5 lakh, compared with its earlier average of 2.5 lakh.Mumbai's average daily passenger footfall increased to 1.6 lakh from around 1 lakh, reflecting the heightened demand for rail travel during the festive season.
Article Summary: Delhi, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Surat recorded the highest outward passenger movement during the current festive rush. Around 57 lakh passengers travelled from 16 railway stations across these regions between November 1 and 6. Around 30 lakh of these passengers had reserved tickets, while 27 lakh travelled in unreserved classes.

Article Title: ‘Loads more ahead’: British High Commission in India hails trade deal amid Diwali celebrations
Article Text:
India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA)

NEW DELHI: The British High Commission in India marked Diwali by highlighting the landmark India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA), saying the deal has given the two countries more reasons to celebrate and expressing optimism about the future of their partnership.In a post on X, the High Commission said this year’s Diwali celebrations were especially bright following the delivery of the trade agreement."The Diwali smiles are extra bright at this year! With our landmark Free Trade Agreement delivered and loads more ahead for the modern UK-India partnership, we had loads to celebrate. HappyDiwali to everyone celebrating!" the British High Commission in India said.The celebrations come after the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) came into effect in July, marking a step towards closer trade and investment ties between the two countries.The agreement aims to expand economic ties through improved market access, trade liberalisation and tariff concessions.Under the deal, nearly 99% of Indian exports will receive zero-duty access to the UK, covering almost 100% of their trade value. It is expected to improve the competitiveness of Indian exports, boost bilateral trade and investment, and create opportunities for businesses.The agreement also includes one of the most ambitious commitments on services that the UK has offered under a free trade agreement.Several foreign diplomatic missions in India also celebrated Diwali with their staff, sharing glimpses of the festivities on social media.Japan’s Ambassador to India, Ono Keiichi, celebrated the festival with Indian and Japanese colleagues at the Embassy of Japan. The occasion marked his third Diwali in the country.Sharing a video of the celebrations, Ono said celebrating with embassy staff had made the festival even more memorable. The video showed traditional diyas, colourful rangoli designs and marigold decorations, with employees dressed in traditional Indian attire."Celebrated Diwali with all the Embassy staff! Sharing the joy of this beautiful festival with both Indian and Japanese colleagues made my 3rd Diwali in India even more memorable. Happy Diwali!!" ONO Keiichi wrote.The French Embassy in India also shared a video of its annual Diwali celebrations, featuring embassy staff and French Ambassador to India Thierry Mathou.Posted on X on Friday, the 93-second video showed employees preparing for the festival before the ceremonial lighting of a brass diya decorated with marigold flowers. Mathou was also seen lighting the lamp and extending greetings."Diwali is a beautiful celebration of life, hope and new beginnings. May this festival bring joy to every home and continue to strengthen the bonds of friendship between France and India," he added.
Article Summary: The British High Commission in India marked Diwali by highlighting the landmark India-UK Free Trade Agreement (FTA) The High Commission said this year’s celebrations were especially bright following the delivery of the trade agreement. Several foreign diplomatic missions in India also celebrated the festival with their staff, sharing glimpses of the festivities.

Article Title: 'E20 petrol by PSU firms meets prescribed quality standards': Oil ministry rejects Karnataka charge
Article Text:
Oil ministry's findings contradict Karnataka's claims of higher-than-permitted ethanol levels in petrol samples

NEW DELHI: The petroleum ministry on Saturday rejected Karnataka's allegations of excessive ethanol content in petrol sold at some retail outlets, saying tests conducted by state-run oil companies found all 893 samples collected across 27 states and Union territories compliant with prescribed quality standards. The findings included 56 samples from Karnataka, which recorded ethanol content between 19 and 20 per cent.In a statement, the ministry said Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) tested the samples and found ethanol levels within the prescribed 19-21 per cent range under the Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 17021 specification. The Karnataka samples had an average ethanol content of 19.30 per cent, it added, news agency PTI reported.The findings contradict Karnataka's statement, which claimed that samples collected from certain fuel stations in October 2026 contained 26-31 per cent ethanol.The three oil marketing companies (OMCs) have questioned the state's sampling and testing procedures, saying the results cannot be independently verified without complete documentation and compliance with prescribed statutory procedures. They said they were not provided with retention samples, outlet-wise details or complete laboratory reports despite seeking them through the state level coordinator.The companies also flagged discrepancies in certificates issued by a third-party laboratory, arguing that the documents did not specify the test method, dilution procedure or reference material used to determine ethanol content through Gas Chromatography. They have sought access to counterpart samples for independent testing at an authorised laboratory in the presence of state officials and OMC representatives.The controversy comes amid concerns over the nationwide rollout of E20 petrol, which contains 20 per cent ethanol, including questions about vehicle mileage, engine compatibility and repair costs. The ministry said the impact on mileage varies according to vehicle category and engine calibration. Vehicles calibrated for E20 could see a reduction of around 1-2 per cent, while some other vehicles could experience a decline of 3-6 per cent.The OMCs have also disputed estimates that E20 could result in annual mileage losses worth Rs 62,000 crore and vehicle repair expenses of Rs 39,000 crore. They said applying a blanket assumption of 10 per cent mileage loss across all vehicles was not scientifically established and sought supporting performance data and repair-cost records.Defending the programme, the ministry cited its contribution to energy security, lower crude oil imports and agricultural incomes. Since the 2014-15 ethanol supply year, the initiative has resulted in foreign exchange savings of more than Rs 1.97 lakh crore, substitution of approximately 316 lakh metric tonnes of crude oil and payments exceeding Rs 1.66 lakh crore to farmers, according to ministry figures.The OMCs said more than 30 crore two-wheelers and four crore four-wheelers have been using E20 fuel for over three years, with no reported widespread vehicle breakdowns attributable to fuel quality. They also rejected suggestions that they had a commercial incentive to exceed prescribed ethanol blending levels, saying additional procurement would increase their costs.
Article Summary: Oil ministry's findings contradict Karnataka's claims of higher-than-permitted ethanol levels in petrol samples. Karnataka samples had an average ethanol content of 19.30 per cent, it added. The controversy comes amid concerns over the nationwide rollout of E20 petrol, which contains 20 per cent ethanol.

Article Title: Coca-Cola's Indian bottling business files for IPO; 99.75 crore shares up for sale
Article Text:
Coca-Cola's India bottling arm files IPO papers

HCCH's beverage portfolio and distribution network

Who owns HCCH?

HCCB's manufacturing footprint in India

NEW DELHI: The Coca-Cola Company's Indian bottling business, Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), has initiated the process for a stock market listing by filing its draft IPO papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi).The proposed initial public offering (IPO) will involve the sale of up to 99.75 crore equity shares by promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6. The issue will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS), which means HCCH will not receive any money from the IPO. All proceeds will go to the selling shareholder.The filing follows Coca-Cola's statement in June that it was exploring a potential listing of HCCH in 2027. HCCH is the parent entity of Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB), the company's Indian bottling arm.HCCH operates across three beverage categories: sparkling, hydration and stills, including juices. Its activities include preparing, packaging, distributing and selling beverages, with its portfolio comprising 41 products as of June 30, 2026.The company had a distribution network spanning around 1.7 million retail outlets, supported by 2,273 distributors, as of June 30, 2026.The TKC Report cited in the DRHP identifies HCCH as the largest non-alcoholic ready-to-drink (NARTD) beverage company by revenue among businesses operating exclusively in India in FY26. It also ranks the company as the largest bottler within the Coca-Cola System in India, based on units of concentrate sold.HCCH's retained units reported revenue from operations of Rs 4,310.17 crore for the three months ended June 30, 2026, registering a year-on-year increase of 20.46 per cent. Total sales volume grew 18.61 per cent over the same period.The Coca-Cola Company held a 60 per cent stake in HCCH through Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd as of the DRHP filing date. The remaining 40 per cent was owned by Jubilant Beverages Ltd, which became one of HCCH's promoters in July 2025.The proposed listing also comes amid Coca-Cola's global asset-light strategy, under which the beverage major has been divesting its bottling assets. India is its fifth-largest market globally.In 2024, the company transferred its bottling operations in Rajasthan, Bihar, the Northeast and parts of West Bengal to existing bottlers through franchise arrangements. These transactions generated $290 million (around Rs 2,420 crore) for Coca-Cola.Kandhari Global Beverages, SLMG Beverages and Moon Beverages were awarded the franchises.Coca-Cola operates in India through two entities: Coca-Cola India and Hindustan Coca-Cola Beverages (HCCB). Incorporated in February 1997, HCCB operates 14 bottling plants across the country.The company is headquartered in Bengaluru, with operations spread across 10 states. Its manufacturing and sales portfolio includes Coca-Cola, Thums Up, Sprite, Minute Maid, Maaza, SmartWater, Kinley, Limca and Fanta, among others.Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, Citigroup Global Markets India, JP Morgan India, Morgan Stanley India Company, Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs (India) Securities and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.
Article Summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH) files its draft IPO papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India. The proposed initial public offering (IPO) will involve the sale of up to 99.75 crore equity shares. The issue will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS), which means HCCH will not receive any money from the IPO. All proceeds will go to the selling shareholder.

Article Title: Stuck at work on Diwali? Firms offer employees longer breaks, better gifts and extra earnings
Article Text:
AI generated image, used only for representational purpose

Gifts employees actually want

WFH for those traveling home

When the festive spirit has to reach the workplace

Diwali duty comes with extra earnings

Stuck at a desk while the rest of the world is busy celebrating may not be the ideal Diwali plan. However, companies are rolling out a range of festive perks to make sure their employees don't miss out on the celebrations.From longer weekends and work-from-home options to gifts of their choice and office festivities, employers are finding different ways to make the festival special for their workforce.And for those who have to work while others celebrate, there are extra payouts and special treats to sweeten the deal.For employees at quick-commerce firm Zepto, the festive break has come a day earlier than scheduled. The company advanced its holiday from Tuesday to Monday, giving its workforce an additional day off after Diwali."We want our people to enjoy the festive season with their families by giving them a longer weekend to celebrate," Sneha Arora, chief HR officer at the Bengaluru-headquartered firm told ET.At Hitachi India, employees had the opportunity to decide what they wanted as their festive gifts. The diversified manufacturer asked them to vote from a list of options, with air fryers and Amazon gift vouchers emerging as popular choices.Festive celebrations at the company also extended beyond gifts. Hitachi India hosted gatherings at hotels across the country, bringing together its Indian and Japanese employees, including senior leadership, said chief human resources officer Ashutosh Anshu.For employees planning to travel during Diwali, flexibility over where they work has also become part of the festive arrangements.Hitachi India's hybrid work policy allows employees to work from home for two days a week. This gives them room to manage festive travel and personal commitments, Anshu said.Aditya Mishra, chief executive at staffing and recruitment services firm CIEL HR Services, said greater flexibility in how employees celebrate has been a noticeable trend this festive season.Companies are extending work-from-home options wherever the nature of the job allows it, particularly for employees who want to travel to their hometowns but continue working."more work-from-home options are given wherever the nature of the role permits, to help employees who wish to travel to their hometowns and continue working", he said.Not everyone gets to switch off during Diwali. Employees working in housekeeping, security, office support, electrical and maintenance roles may still need to keep offices functioning during the celebrations.Proptech firm NoBroker.com is organising special festivities for these teams, along with a role-reversal exercise involving its HR department.Under the initiative, HR employees will take on the responsibilities usually handled by support staff for a few hours. This includes staffing office floors, managing security and ensuring that operations continue, allowing the employees in these roles to participate in the celebrations."For those few hours, our HR team steps into their shoes, staffing the floors, managing security and keeping the offices running, so that not a single person has to miss the festivities," said chief executive Amit Kumar Agarwal.For employees whose work involves being on the road, festive celebrations are also taking the form of additional financial incentives.Trev Mobility, an electric vehicles-focused cab-hailing service, has introduced a special incentive programme for its driver-partners working during Diwali, according to ET. The additional payouts will be over and above their regular earnings for working on designated festive days, said founder Naveen Gupta.The amount drivers can earn will depend on how many days they choose to work. Those available for just one or two days can also qualify for additional earnings, while driver-partners who complete all four designated days of duty, including Diwali, will be eligible for a significantly enhanced payout.Under the programme, those completing all four days will receive double payment, Gupta said."The incentive is structured around the number of days they choose to work, so even those available for one or two days can earn extra. Those who complete all four designated days of duty, including Diwali, are eligible for a significantly enhanced payout, with double payment under the programme," he added.
Article Summary: Employers are rolling out a range of festive perks to make sure their employees don't miss out on the celebrations. From longer weekends and work-from-home options to gifts of their choice and office festivities, employers are finding different ways to make the festival special for their workforce.
